Fix, bound or equate parameters, and test the indirect effect with one call.
Part of the [Models](models.html) collection; the third of five
[native engine](model-native.html) pages.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it does** | equality, inequality and fixed-value constraints on labeled paths, linear or nonlinear; `mbco_sem()` for the indirect effect; `anova()` for nested fits |
| **Class returned** | `SEMFit` |
| **Syntax** | `a == b`, `a + b == 1`, `a < 0.3`, `y ~ 0.5 * x`, `CONSTRAINT(a == b)` |
| **Limit** | a sum of products such as `a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 == 0` is best-effort (see Limits) |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
"
```

## Equal paths

Write the constraint on its own line, bare or inside `CONSTRAINT()`:

```{r}
#| label: equal
free <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
equal <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "CONSTRAINT(a == b)\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b")], constrained = coef(equal)[c("a", "b")])
```

The constrained fit has one more degree of freedom, and `summary(equal)` lists
the constraint as active under Diagnostics.

## Bounds and fixed values

```{r}
#| label: bounds
bounded <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "a < 0.3\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
round(coef(bounded)[c("a", "b")], 4)

fixed <- fit_sem(sub("cp \\*", "0 *", paste0(base, "ab := a * b")), mediation_demo)
round(coef(fixed)[c("a", "b")], 4)
```

`a < 0.3` pushed `a` onto the bound, and `cp` was fixed at 0 in the second fit.
A parameter that sits on a bound has a standard error of 0 in the table; read the
"Active bounds" line of `summary()` before using it.

## Test the indirect effect

`mbco_sem()` is the minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio test (MBCO): it refits with
`a` fixed at 0 and with `b` fixed at 0, and the smaller statistic tests
$a \, b = 0$.

```{r}
#| label: mbco
mbco_sem(free, "a", "b")
```

The result is an `htest`; the two component tests are in its `tests` element.
For a chain, name every path: `mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b"))` is the
minimum of the single-path tests for $a \, d \, b = 0$, referred to a
chi-square with 1 degree of freedom.

A refit that cannot be fitted does not stop `mbco_sem()`. This happens, for example,
when the null `a = 0` contradicts a constraint already in the model (`a > 0.3`). The failed
refit is a row of `tests` with `converged = FALSE` and the reason in `note`, a warning repeats
it, and the statistic and p-value are `NA` rather than the smaller of the refits that worked.
Check `res$unresolved` before reading the p-value; the
[troubleshooting guide](guide-troubleshooting.html#an-unresolved-mbco-result) shows the
result.

## Nonlinear constraints

A constraint may be nonlinear in the labels. Setting `cp` equal to the indirect
effect is one:

```{r}
#| label: nonlinear
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "CONSTRAINT(cp == a * b)\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
```

## Compare nested fits

`anova()` is the likelihood-ratio test for two nested `SEMFit`s and refits
nothing; you vouch that the restriction is nested in substance.

```{r}
#| label: anova
anova(tied, free)
```

## Limits

- **Nonlinear constraints are solved with their Jacobian recomputed at every
  point.** `cp == a * b` and `a * b > 0.1` work; a nonlinear inequality can be
  feasible on several disjoint pieces (`a * b > 0.1` holds for two positive or
  two negative paths), so every start is tried and the best one kept, with a
  warning when the starts disagree. A sum of products such as
  `a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 == 0` is best-effort (no exact reduction exists): treat the
  fit as the best of the starts, and raise `n_starts` when the warning appears.
- **A constraint needs a free parameter** and **labels must be defined** in the
  model.
- **Equal labels are one parameter.** Giving two paths the same label equates them
  without a constraint line.
